title: Weighted skill-curve allocation for cycle surge and scoped degradation
creator: Aditi Shah
description: Create a repeatable, quantitative allocation mechanism that maps available engineering capacity to active initiatives using weighted skill-curves. The mechanism should support dynamic surge credits, conditional scope degradation (soft-freeze triggers), and clear roll-forward rules so PMs can make deterministic scope cuts without manual arbitration during mid-cycle capacity shocks.
background: We repeatedly struggle with mid-cycle bursts where teams must make ad-hoc scope cuts. Existing playbooks are qualitative (priority lanes, tranche buckets). This ticket experiments with a mathematical layer: each role/engineer is represented by a skill vector; initiatives submit a skill demand profile; allocation uses a weighted-skill-match curve and a surge-credit budget to proportionally distribute fractional capacity. The aim is to reduce subjective net-new decisions and speed mid-cycle rebalances.
goals: Design a weighted skill-curve model that outputs fractional FTE allocation per initiative given a pool of engineers
Define soft-freeze trigger thresholds and automated scope degradation rules (percentage-based) for low-priority slices
Draft PM playbook and tooling checklist for executing a mid-cycle redistribution using the model
Run a dry-run on Q2 mid-sprint scenario with one product area and one infra area and measure decision latency improvement
success_metrics: Decision latency for mid-cycle scope cuts reduced from median 6 hours to <1 hour
Stakeholder satisfaction (survey) >= 70% for fairness of rebalancing decisions
Number of ad-hoc reassignments reduced by 40% compared to previous cycle
Automated allocation match rate >= 85% of team-reported ideal allocations in dry-run
acceptance_criteria: Calculation engine prototype (spreadsheet + script) that ingests skill profiles and outputs allocations
Documented soft-freeze trigger matrix with 3 trigger levels and corresponding percent-scope-degrade rules
One runbook (step-by-step) that a PM can follow during a surge, including stakeholder comms templates
Dry-run results and retrospective with lessons and a recommended policy to adopt for next cycle
implementation_notes: Prototype in a Google Sheet first to make curves visible to PMs and Eng leads
Representation: skill vectors are normalized; match score = dot(skills, demand) / sqrt(|demand|)
Surge credits: assign per-team monthly credit pool that can be burned to preserve priority allocations; credits expire at cycle end
Tooling: short-term use of a script (Python) to convert sheet -> JSON -> visual allocation summary; long-term consider adding to internal capacity dashboard
timeline: 2026-02-28: Review with Eng leads and adjust skill taxonomy
2026-03-05: Build python exporter and run first dry-run scenario
2026-03-12: PM/Eng retrospective on dry-run; iterate acceptance criteria
2026-03-22: Finalize playbook and recommend policy for Q3 cycle adoption
stakeholders: Data analyst for metrics: Maria Gomez
risks: Overfitting skill taxonomy to current team composition -> will fail as hires change
Resistance from orgs that prefer manual negotiation; may reduce perceived autonomy
Modelic allocations may ignore cross-pairing needs (onboarding, domain knowledge)
Surge credits could be gamed if not auditable; requires simple governance and dashboards
decisions: Use normalized dot-product skill-match for first iteration (transparent in sheet)
Surge credits are per-team, not per-person, and burnable only via PM sign-off
Soft-freeze will degrade scope in 10% increments at each trigger level (10/30/60)
Adopt prototype only as recommended policy after two successful dry-runs and a stakeholder signoff
